contract: Bounded volatile local computation under an injected Task.Supervisor: a per-owner controller serializes completion, DOWN, cancel and monotonic deadlines, counts tasks through actual termination and offers one caller-wrapped outcome through the owner's current Registry name. Cancel brutally kills active tasks; success processed at or after deadline is timed_out. Owner-only restart preserves controller tracking but the replacement owner rejects unknown actions as late; controller restart loses tracking. No queue, durable delivery, retry or engine policy.
limits: Trusted bounded non-Effect computations and prompt nonblocking wraps; no OTP sandbox or bound on memory, mailboxes, descendants or orphans after untrappable controller kill.
Offers can be lost on absent owner, send race or wrap failure; no acknowledgement, retry, buffer or durable cancellation receipt. Loss does not prove work never ran or undo an Effect.

Caller supplies a unique Registry, Task.Supervisor and one independently supervised controller per owner, an owner-side late-result gate, and subtree teardown before reestablishing capacity after controller restart.
Refs and monotonic deadlines are runtime-local and volatile. Settled refs are removed without history; call/startup timeout after dispatch is uncertain. Telemetry is planned, with no events supplied.

grounding.claim: AW1 free owner/completion; AW2 cancel, racing result and receiver late gate; AW3 sanitized raise/throw/exit/kill losses and legitimate completed value; AW4 deadline kill including trap-exit and queued late success; AW5 owner-only replacement versus controller restart; AW6 bound, invalid/missing/full refusal, concurrent admission and shutdown; AW7 lost offers, raising wrap and settled duplicate signals. Finite scenarios, not universal proofs.
Pinned Elixir 1.20.4 Task.Supervisor async_nolink, Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill), GenServer serialization and unique Registry name resolution.
Pinned OTP 29.1.2 process monitors, kill signals, absolute monotonic timers and cancellation; scheduling is not an exact-time delivery guarantee.

Caller-owned independent supervision, bounded non-Effect computation, prompt trusted wrap, unique Registry and owner-side late-result/recovery policy. Host tears down predecessor tasks before replacing a controller's capacity. No Cure proof, independent type-check or production monitoring claimed.

telemetry.contract: No events supplied; library diagnostics contain no payload, wrapped message or exception contents. Consumer functions own their logging.

config.contract: Start-time owner Registry name, injected Task.Supervisor, positive integer max_concurrency and optional OTP name; per-work zero-arity computation, arity-2 wrap and timeout in 1..4_294_967_295 ms. No hot changes.

control.contract: cancel/2 kills active work before releasing capacity and offers killed once; unknown/settled/previous-controller refs return late. No pause, drain or durable receipt.
